text:
Shea Theodore's season is a good test of whether you trust the box score or the play. The box score says seven points in 21 games, no goals in his last ten, and our wins added has him near the bottom of the league (510th of 528), mostly because the moments that swung games haven't involved him.

The play says something else. Vegas takes 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, seven points better than without him, and his on-ice luck is about neutral. His own shooting is right in line with his chances. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at the 87th percentile among defensemen last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him, well above a typical defenseman's 11%.

So why so few points? Some of it is the power play, where he has only two points while others run the top unit. He's playing more lately (23 minutes a night over the last ten), which is the coaches telling you what they think. We'd expect the assists to start showing up.
